item.title: Quick Take — Frontiers of Statistics in Science and Engineering: 2035 and Beyond
item.description: This is a consensus report assessing where the field of statistics stands, where its most important frontiers lie, and what investments the United States needs to sustain those frontiers through 2035 and beyond. The central argument is that statistics is a generative force in science and engineering, co-producing discoveries rather than merely analyzing data after the fact. Written as AI has become dominant in research and industry, the report maintains throughout that many of the hardest open problems in AI, including interpretability, uncertainty quantification, robustness, and calibration, are fundamentally statistical problems.

item.title: Ch. 1 — Summary
item.description: Statistics is the science through which data become wisdom. Scientific and engineering progress is driven by statistical innovation, and the field continues to evolve through reciprocal interaction with scientific discovery. With the influx of computing capacity, proliferation and interoperability of data, and the availability of increasingly complex modeling, the statistical landscape is shifting in ways that will transform its demands and broaden its contributions. This report illustrates the role of statistics as a key element of science and engineering progress, and presents selected key findings, conclusions, and recommendations that underscore the report's main message.

item.title: Ch. 1 — Summary
item.description: Statistics is the science through which data become wisdom. Scientific and engineering progress is driven by statistical innovation, and the field continues to evolve through reciprocal interaction with scientific innovation. With the influx of computing capacity, proliferation and interoperability of data, and availability of increasingly complex modeling, the statistical landscape is shifting in ways that will transform its demands and broaden its contributions. This report illustrates the role of statistics as a key element of science and engineering progress. Recommendations in the report highlight critical areas of stewardship, capacity-building, and investment in the statistical sciences to sustain and expand the field's contributions for U.S. competitiveness. This summary presents selected key findings, conclusions, and recommendations that underscore the report's main message. (Within the body of the report, key findings, conclusions, and recommendations are numbered according to the chapter number and order of appearance. However, selected key findings, conclusions, and recommendations have been included in the Summary in the order that best preserves narrative flow, which may not align with this numbering scheme.)
